HIV,  Other  STD,  and  Teen  Pregnancy  Prevention  and 
 North  Carolina  Students 
What is the problem? 
The 2011 North Carolina Youth Risk Behavior Survey indicates that among high school students: 
Sexual Risk Behaviors 
•  49% ever had sexual intercourse. 
•  9% had sexual intercourse for the first time before age 13 years. 
•  17% had sexual intercourse with four or more persons during their life. 
•  35% had sexual intercourse with at least one person during the 3 months before the survey. 
• 46%  did  not  use  a  condom  during  last  sexual  intercourse.  (1)    
• — did not use birth control pills or Depo­Provera (or any injectable birth control), Nuva Ring (or any birth control ring), 
implanon  (or  any  implant),  or  any  IUD  before  last  sexual  intercourse.  (1)    
• —  were  never  taught  in  school  about  AIDS or  HIV  infection.    
Alcohol and Other Drug Use 
• 25%  drank  alcohol  or  used  drugs  before  last  sexual  intercourse.  (1)    
• — used a needle to inject any illegal drug into their body one or more times during their life.  
What are the solutions? 
Better health education • More comprehensive health services • More supportive policies • More family involvement 
What is the status? 
The 2012 North Carolina School Health Profiles indicates that among high schools: 
Health Education 
•  17% required students to take 2 or more health education courses. 
•  75% had a health education curriculum that addresses all 8 national standards for health education. 
•  69% taught 9 key pregnancy, HIV, or other STD prevention topics in a required course. 
•  39% taught 4 key topics related to condom use in a required course. 
•  83% taught how to access valid and reliable health information, products, or services related to HIV, other STDs, and 
pregnancy in a required course. 
•  58% had a lead health education teacher who received professional development during the 2 years before the survey 
on HIV prevention. 
•  49% had a lead health education teacher who received professional development during the 2 years before the survey 
on pregnancy prevention. 
Health Services 
•    33%  had  a  full­time  registered  nurse  who  provides  health  services  to  students  at  school.  
Supportive Policies 
•  32% had a gay/straight alliance or similar club. 
•  5% provided curricula or supplementary materials and engaged in 5 practices related to lesbian, gay, bisexual, 
transgender, or questioning (LGBTQ) youth. 
Family Involvement 
•  27% provided parents and families health information to increase parent and family knowledge of HIV prevention, STD 
prevention, or teen pregnancy prevention. 
1. Among  students  who  were  currently  sexually  active.

Data not available.
